subtopics.title: Plot hyperbolas from tables
subtopics.exposition: For h(x) = 1/x, the function is undefined at x = 0; this is called a discontinuity at x = 0. For h(x) = 1/x, the value at x = 0 is 1/0, which is undefined. Since y = h(x) = 1/x, we can write x × y = 1. The graph of h(x) = 1/x lies in the first and third quadrants, because the product of two positive numbers and the product of two negative numbers can both equal 1. For h(x) = 1/x, as x gets larger, h(x) gets closer to, but does not equal, 0; this is a horizontal asymptote, the line y = 0. In the third quadrant, as x gets smaller, h(x) also approaches the negative x-axis asymptotically. For h(x) = 1/x there is a vertical asymptote, the line x = 0; as x gets closer to 0, h(x) approaches the y-axis asymptotically. The graph of h(x) = 1/x has two axes of symmetry, the lines y = x and y = -x; about these two lines one half of the hyperbola is a mirror image of the other half. To complete a table of values for h(x) = 1/x, substitute each given x-value into the equation and calculate h(x), for example h(-3) = 1/(-3) = -1/3. To plot a hyperbola from the table, plot the points that the table gives and join them with two smooth curves.

subtopics.title: Effects of a and q
subtopics.exposition: Functions of the general form y = a/x + q are called hyperbolic functions. The effect of q is called a vertical shift, because all points are moved the same distance in the same direction (it slides the entire graph up or down). For q > 0, the graph of f(x) is shifted vertically upwards by q units. For q < 0, the graph of f(x) is shifted vertically downwards by q units. The horizontal asymptote of y = a/x + q is the line y = q. The vertical asymptote of y = a/x + q is always the y-axis, the line x = 0. The sign of a determines the shape of the graph. If a > 0, the graph of f(x) lies in the first and third quadrants. For a > 1, the graph of f(x) will be further away from the axes than y = 1/x. For 0 < a < 1, as a tends to 0, the graph moves closer to the axes than y = 1/x. If a < 0, the graph of f(x) lies in the second and fourth quadrants. For a < -1, the graph of f(x) will be further away from the axes than y = -1/x. For -1 < a < 0, as a tends to 0, the graph moves closer to the axes than y = -1/x. To investigate the effect of q, plot y = 1/x - 2, y = 1/x - 1, y = 1/x, y = 1/x + 1 and y = 1/x + 2 on the same set of axes and use the results to deduce the effect of q. To investigate the effect of a, plot y = -2/x, y = -1/x, y = 1/x and y = 2/x on the same set of axes and use the results to deduce the effect of a.

subtopics.title: Intercepts, domain and range
subtopics.exposition: For y = a/x + q, the function is undefined for x = 0, so the domain is {x : x in R, x not equal to 0}. The rewritten function is undefined only at y = q. The range of y = a/x + q is {f(x) : f(x) in R, f(x) not equal to q}. For h(x) = 1/x, the range read from the graph is {y : y in R, y not equal to 0}, since y is defined for all values except 0. For g(x) = 2/x + 2, setting x = 0 gives 2/0 + 2, which is undefined, therefore there is no y-intercept. To find the range of y = a/x + q, rewrite the equation to make x the subject: y - q = a/x, then (y - q)x = a for x not equal to 0, then x = a/(y - q). For g(x) = 2/x + 2, the domain is {x : x in R, x not equal to 0} because g(x) is undefined only at x = 0. For g(x) = 2/x + 2, g(x) is undefined only at y = 2, so the range is {g(x) : g(x) in R, g(x) not equal to 2}. To calculate the y-intercept, let x = 0, because every point on the y-axis has an x-coordinate of 0. To calculate the x-intercept, let y = 0, because every point on the x-axis has a y-coordinate of 0. For g(x) = 2/x + 2, setting y = 0 gives 2/x = -2 and x = -1, so the x-intercept is the point (-1, 0).

subtopics.title: Sketch hyperbolic graphs
subtopics.exposition: There are two asymptotes for functions of the form y = a/x + q. The horizontal asymptote is the line y = q and the vertical asymptote is always the y-axis, the line x = 0. A hyperbola of the form y = a/x + q is symmetrical about two lines: y = x + q and y = -x + q. To sketch a graph of the form y = f(x) = a/x + q, determine four characteristics: the sign of a, the y-intercept, the x-intercept and the asymptotes. The four characteristics to determine before sketching are: sign of a, y-intercept, x-intercept, asymptotes. A sketch of a hyperbola marks the intercepts and the asymptotes. Sketching step one: examine the standard form; for g(x) = 2/x + 2, a > 0, therefore the graph lies in the first and third quadrant. Sketching step three: for g(x) = 2/x + 2, the horizontal asymptote is the line y = 2 and the vertical asymptote is the line x = 0. Sketching step one: examine the standard form; for y = -4/x + 7, a < 0, therefore the graph lies in the second and fourth quadrants. Sketching step two: for y = -4/x + 7, letting x = 0 gives an undefined value, therefore there is no y-intercept. Sketching step two: for y = -4/x + 7, letting y = 0 gives -4/x = -7 and x = 4/7, so the x-intercept is the point (4/7, 0). Sketching step three: for y = -4/x + 7, the horizontal asymptote is the line y = 7 and the vertical asymptote is the line x = 0. For y = -4/x + 7, the axes of symmetry are y = x + 7 and y = -x + 7.
